admissibility_boundary_geometry.description: Formal scaffold for the geometry of admissibility boundaries across the Mono-Process Framework.
core_principles: Admissibility is defined by a manifold of valid continuation states bounded by structural singularities.
Boundaries represent transitions from stable process dynamics to undefined or divergent states.
Geometry is defined locally through operator-specific constraints and globally through recursive stability basins.

boundary_classes.name: epsilon_null_singularity_boundary
boundary_classes.description: The exact limit where mismatch epsilon equals zero; represents the boundary of process necessity.
boundary_classes.geometry: Lower-dimensional singularity surface in participation space.

boundary_classes.name: projection_clipping_boundary
boundary_classes.description: The boundary of the Pi_A admissibility window where states are projected to null.

boundary_classes.name: orientation_sensitive_window_boundary
boundary_classes.description: Refinement of the admissibility window based on orientation deviation -(i).

boundary_classes.name: transport_legality_threshold
boundary_classes.description: The limit beyond which NavT transport flux becomes non-convergent or aggregate-erased.
boundary_classes.geometry: Radial decay boundary in the CSI interaction domain.

boundary_classes.name: recursive_stability_boundary
boundary_classes.description: The boundary of the stable basin for iterative process updates.
boundary_classes.geometry: Attractor basin boundary in recursive state space.

boundary_classes.name: branch_retention_boundary
boundary_classes.description: The transition point where multi-branch retention (delta) must be pruned to avoid explosion.
boundary_classes.geometry: Complexity-threshold boundary in the branching tree.

boundary_classes.name: numerical_stability_boundary
boundary_classes.description: Implementation-induced limits (e.g., Euler step bounds) that constrain admissible simulation.
boundary_classes.geometry: Step-size and precision dependent stability surface.
